STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate with a rim band and a flat centre, with no inner wall or shadow. This is a flat square plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are 20-30 cm. This one looks like a standard dinner-size square plate, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference: the chicken pieces are roughly 10-11 cm long, and the plate spans about 2.5 to 3 of those lengths across its width, giving about 26-28 cm. Reconciling both cues, width ≈ 26 cm (area ≈ 676 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Chicken (breaded, baked): two pieces covering roughly 22% of the plate, about 150 cm². Average thickness: a breast piece is about 2-2.5 cm, so use 2 cm. Volume = 300 ml; at 1.0 g/ml, about 300 g. Breaded chicken is somewhat less dense than raw meat, so take about 230 g.
- Caesar-style salad (romaine leaves with creamy dressing and some croutons or cheese): covers roughly 20% of the plate, about 135 cm². Loose leaves stacked 3-4 cm at the centre, averaging about 2 cm. Volume ≈ 270 ml. Dressed leafy greens at about 0.3 g/ml (dressing adds weight) gives about 80 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the chicken has no visible base layer and the salad sits directly on the plate, so no extra items are added.

STEP 5 - Energy:
- Breaded baked chicken: about 200 kcal per 100 g.
- Caesar salad with dressing: about 150 kcal per 100 g (dressing is energy-dense).

Totals: about 310 g and roughly 530 kcal.
